answer: A container-terminal yard planner resists sybils the way it resists a fake stack tide: each AI agent must occupy a verified physical slot, bonded by a staked container token that can only be rehandled once per epoch. Any whisper of a duplicate identity triggers a yard audit that cross-checks crane-move provenance against slot history, forcing attackers to pay rehandling costs for every cloned slot. This sonnet of stacked proofs fails when colluders control real slots, so throughput caps and randomized reshuffles bound the damage.
